headline: 6 killed in fire at Cox’s Bazar resort
summary: Six bodies were recovered from the Tuptup Resto & Resort in Inani Beach, Ukhiya, after a devastating blaze that burnt the wooden structure to charcoal.
details: Six people have died after a fire broke out at the Tuptup Resto & Resort in the Patuartek area of Inani Beach, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, this morning.
Four other people were injured in the incident and are currently receiving treatment at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital.
The Ukhiya Fire Service station dispatched two units to the scene after receiving information about the fire at 7:25 am, bringing the blaze under control by 11:00 am.
Syed Mohammad Morshed Hossain, deputy assistant director of Cox’s Bazar Fire Service, stated that the three-storey wooden resort was completely burnt to charcoal.
According to fire service officials, the injured suffered various burns and injuries sustained while attempting to escape the fire.
The cause of the fire and the identities of the deceased have not yet been determined.
caption:
6 people killed and 4 injured after a devastating fire destroys a resort in Cox's Bazar.

Six people have died after a fire broke out at the Tuptup Resto & Resort in the Patuartek area of Inani Beach, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, this morning.

Four other people were injured in the incident and are currently receiving treatment at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital.

The Ukhiya Fire Service station dispatched two units to the scene after receiving information about the fire at 7:25 am, bringing the blaze under control by 11:00 am.

Syed Mohammad Morshed Hossain, deputy assistant director of Cox’s Bazar Fire Service, stated that the three-storey wooden resort was completely burnt to charcoal.

According to fire service officials, the injured suffered various burns and injuries sustained while attempting to escape the fire.

The cause of the fire and the identities of the deceased have not yet been determined.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman visits hospitals and schools to assess dengue situation in Dhaka
summary: The Prime Minister conducted surprise visits to medical facilities and educational institutions to monitor cleanliness and dengue prevention measures.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman conducted surprise visits to several hospitals and educational institutions in Dhaka this morning to assess the dengue situation and cleanliness activities.
The Prime Minister first visited the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital in Uttara to review the measures taken by authorities to tackle the disease.
He also visited Rajuk Uttara Model College, where he addressed members of the Bangladesh National Cadet Corps (BNCC) and urged them to play an active role in cleanliness drives.
The Prime Minister's itinerary includes further visits to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and various hospitals under the Dhaka North and South city corporations.
On September 12, the Prime Minister launched a three-month special campaign to prevent dengue, focusing on cleanliness drives and public awareness activities.
Considering the next three months as a high-risk period, he has urged citizens across the country to actively participate in the campaign to prevent the spread of the virus.
caption:
PM Tarique Rahman conducts surprise visits to Dhaka hospitals and schools to monitor dengue prevention.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman conducted surprise visits to several hospitals and educational institutions in Dhaka this morning to assess the dengue situation and cleanliness activities.

The Prime Minister first visited the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital in Uttara to review the measures taken by authorities to tackle the disease.

He also visited Rajuk Uttara Model College, where he addressed members of the Bangladesh National Cadet Corps (BNCC) and urged them to play an active role in cleanliness drives.

The Prime Minister's itinerary includes further visits to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and various hospitals under the Dhaka North and South city corporations.

On September 12, the Prime Minister launched a three-month special campaign to prevent dengue, focusing on cleanliness drives and public awareness activities.

Considering the next three months as a high-risk period, he has urged citizens across the country to actively participate in the campaign to prevent the spread of the virus.
